newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF gives details on investment portfolio.
newsitem.headline: AGF gives details on investment portfolio.

text.p: Assurances Generales de France (AGF) said on Thursday investments managed by the group had a book value of 249.3 billion and a market value of 266.4 billion as of June 30, 1996.

The insurer, which reported a 48.5 percent jump in first half profit to 723 million francs, said bonds made up 66.5 percent of its investment portfolio, equities 18.3 percent and property 15.2 percent.

It said it had pursued a policy of reducing the rate of realisation of capital gains over the first half of 1996. Capital gains in the first half fell by around 32 percent to 1.11 billion francs compared with 1.65 billion in the first half of 1995.

At the same time, boosted by a strong performance by financial markets, unrealised capital gains rose by nearly 15 percent over the six months to 17.1 billion francs at the end of the first half of 1996 from 14.9 billion at the end of December 1995.
